_comment: Committed PDK defaults for design/netlist.py. Environment variables win
over this file, and design/pdk.local.json (git-ignored) wins over both.
variant       sky130 flavor directory to use (sky130A / sky130B)
search_roots  extra directories that CONTAIN variant dirs, searched
before the built-in list (~/.volare, ~/.ciel, ...)
open_pdks_commit is a provenance pin, not a hard gate: netlist.py records
it in --check output so a netlist diff caused by a PDK bump is
distinguishable from one caused by a schematic edit. It matches the pin
spec/porting-plan.md cites and the one the sibling sky130-bandgap repo
uses in its own sim/pdk.json.
This file deliberately does NOT describe the simulation harness (corner
lists, ngspice library paths). sim/ has its own harness and its own
sim/pdk.json, kept deliberately separate from this file rather than
merged or repointed -- see sim/pdk.json's own comment block for the
rationale.
xschem_version_min is a HARD GATE, unlike open_pdks_commit above, and
the two fields below are the design/ counterparts of layout/pdk.json's
klt_version_pin / ci_klt_install pair (issue #151).
xschem_version_min  lowest xschem release whose netlister output this
repo will accept. netlist.py refuses to export or
--check below it rather than emitting a netlist
that cannot be simulated.
ci_xschem_install   what .github/workflows/pdk-nightly.yml's
netlist-check job actually does to satisfy that
floor on ubuntu-latest.
Why a floor exists at all, when open_pdks_commit deliberately is not one:
sky130's xschem device symbols carry their device-area parameters as
expr() templates over the symbol's own @W/@nf attributes, e.g.
ad=expr('int((@nf + 2)/2) * @W / @nf * 0.29'). xschem 3.4.7 is the first
release that EVALUATES those templates at netlist time (its Changelog:
'evaluate infix expressions with expr(...) in attributes', 'Add
eval_expr.y ... (expr(...) in attributes)'). Every earlier release --
including the 3.4.4-1 that ubuntu-noble's `apt-get install xschem`
resolves, which is what pdk-nightly installed until issue #151 -- copies
the template through verbatim, @-attributes and all. So the netlist a
pre-3.4.7 xschem produces is not a differently-formatted netlist, it is
a BROKEN one: ngspice rejects it outright with 'Undefined parameter
[ad]' / 'Cannot compute substitute' and 'ERROR: fatal error in ngspice,
exit(1)' (measured 2026-09-18, ngspice-46, against the pinned
open_pdks_commit's own sky130.lib.spice). Every design/*.spice is
.include'd by testbenches under sim/, so 'regenerate and commit the
diff' -- the remedy pdk-nightly.yml's header comment used to prescribe
for any xschem version bump -- would have silently replaced a simulable
netlist library with an unsimulable one, and netlist.py --check (which
verifies staleness and ERC, never simulability) would have gone green on
it. Hence a floor, enforced in netlist.py, rather than a provenance note.
The floor is a MINIMUM, not an equality pin: a future xschem that
reformats its output is still meant to turn --check red loudly, and the
remedy for THAT is still to regenerate and commit the diff.
The committed design/*.spice were generated and verified with xschem
3.4.7 (the latest tagged release as of 2026-09-18).
ci_xschem_install: build from source at tag 3.4.7 (https://github.com/StefanSchippers/xschem); ubuntu-noble's packaged xschem is 3.4.4-1, below the floor
